cefrAlignment: Matches the B1 phonological-control descriptor (generally intelligible, can approximate word and sentence stress): it uses common words, simple stress patterns and short sentences, and the tasks are recognition and controlled repetition.
examFidelity: The IELTS Part 1 task (no prep, about 30 s) and the TOEIC Read a text aloud tip (45 s prep) match exams.ts; the TOEFL Listen and Repeat tip now cites only what ETS says (accurate, clearly intelligible speech).
fixes: Changed photographer to the dictionary syllable split pho-TOG-ra-pher everywhere (learn, examples, walkthrough, MCQ options, checklist). The lesson had pho-TO-gra-pher next to pho-TOG-ra-phy.
Minimal-pair item 4 'She drives a white van/fan' did not follow the instruction that both words make sense; changed it to 'We bought a new van/fan'.
Changed item 8 from 'costs fifteen pounds', where stress shift before 'pounds' blurs fif-TEEN, to 'The bus leaves at four fifteen', and rewrote the explanation (long /iː/, final /n/, final stress).
Added pen/pan (/e/ vs /æ/) to the Learn section, because ex2 tested it without teaching it.
Added a note that the IPA symbols are British and that American speakers also pronounce the r in work.
The walkthrough now quotes the transcript exactly ('an online course', 'it was really interesting'), adds ex-PEC-ted, and marks 'uh-fuh-TOG-ruh-fuh' as British English.
Rewrote the TOEFL tip: removed the unverified claim that a word with wrong stress 'may be scored as incorrect'; it now cites ETS's construct of accurate, clearly intelligible speech.
Corrected the 'consonant' definition (the air is stopped or blocked, not only 'partly' stopped).
Renamed the model speaker from Daniel to Sam, because TTS voice gender is random.
openConcerns: The minimal-pair and fifteen/fifty items rely on browser TTS. A specialist should check that common US and UK voices really make the /ɪ/–/iː/, /e/–/æ/, /ʌ/–/æ/, /ɜː/–/ɔː/ and final-stress contrasts. Recorded audio would be safer.
Audio uses the default US voice while the IPA symbols are British. This is explained in the text now, but setting voice 'uk' or adding recordings would make them consistent.
learnerOutcome: A learner can hear and say six common vowel and consonant contrasts and put the main stress on everyday multi-syllable words, including the noun/verb pair RE-cord / re-CORD and -teen/-ty numbers.
